sub_questions: What project ideas suit B.Tech ECE students, organized across the core ECE sub-domains (analog/circuits, digital/VLSI, embedded/IoT, communication/RF/antennas, signal & image processing, power electronics, robotics/control, AI/ML at the edge)?
Which projects fit which academic level (mini project in 2nd/3rd year vs final-year major project) and what difficulty, cost, and time does each involve?
What hardware, software, and simulation tools (e.g. LTspice, MATLAB/Simulink, Proteus, Xilinx Vivado, Arduino/ESP32/STM32, Raspberry Pi) do these projects use?
How should a student choose, scope, and execute an ECE project (evaluation criteria used by universities such as AICTE/NBA outcomes, originality, documentation, publishability)?
Which current/trending areas (IoT, edge AI/TinyML, EV & renewable power electronics, 5G/SDR, FPGA/RISC-V, biomedical electronics) make stronger final-year projects?
required_formats: categorized catalog of project ideas with per-project fields (tables)
required_section_headings: ## 1. How to Choose a B.Tech ECE Project
## 3. Mini Projects vs Final-Year Major Projects
scope_conditions: undergraduate B.Tech level (Indian engineering curriculum context) in Electronics and Communication Engineering; all ECE sub-domains, not only one

levers.domain_notes: Sourcing: university/AICTE curriculum and project guidelines, IEEE student/conference papers, vendor application notes (TI, Analog Devices, Espressif, Xilinx), and reputable electronics education sites; low-quality project-selling listicles only as evidence of what is common, never as authority. Evidence norms: prefer projects with documented implementations or published papers; note component cost and feasibility. Recency: last ~3 years for trending topics; fundamentals are timeless.

rationale.register: bare noun-phrase query asks for the landscape of project options, no verdict requested
rationale.inference_depth: widely documented topic; authoritative consensus suffices
